name: Dusty maroon
lede: Dusty maroon is a dark reddish brown, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Hihada-iro, "cypress bark color."

sections.title: Cypress bark
sections.body:
Hihada-iro (檜皮色) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for the bark of the Japanese cypress, *hinoki*, long used in Japan for roofing thatch [1]. The color recalls the bark's weathered reddish brown rather than the pale wood beneath it [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[mahogany]] and [[oxheart]], at Both sit in the library's Reds family alongside the core color [[red|Red]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 1,280 of 23,781 paintings, about 5.4 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is the same Maya mural fragment, dated to about 500, that also matches [[dusty-crimson|Dusty crimson]], here covering closer to two-fifths of the image, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The rate peaks in a small sample of 109 paintings from the 1450s, more than four and a half times the archive's overall rate for that decade [2]. Among sampled painters, Andrea del Sarto's twenty-one paintings contain it eight times, ahead of Sandro Botticelli and Paolo Veronese [2]. It is also disproportionately present in paintings from Tibet and Italy [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
